instructions: Development trials only. Load the selected Shipmate skill and its required references. Give the agent one brief plus its evidence, without the companion rubric. No live tracker, GitLab or repository writes are authorized. Observe the next response; these cases are not production accuracy estimates. For cases with next_user_message, observe the first response before supplying that message and then observe how the answer is applied; keep expected observations in the separate rubric.

cases.brief: Draft a short specification for task completion. TODO and DONE are our literal status names. A task owner may complete their own TODO task, making it DONE. Other users receive the existing forbidden result. These decisions are settled. Draft only.
cases.evidence: The existing task service already verifies ownership. The accepted decision says to reuse it and preserve forbidden behavior. No new ownership mechanism or status vocabulary is needed. The assembled draft has not been confirmed yet.

cases.brief: Specify automatic retries for failed document publication. Draft only.
cases.evidence: The sender can time out after the destination has accepted the document. The destination's deduplication behavior is unknown. A confirmed rejection and an unknown outcome are currently different states. No decision authorizes replaying unknown outcomes, creating new document IDs or promising exactly-once delivery.

cases.brief: Describe the smallest implementation and verification plan for accepting report widths 64 through 120 inclusive. This is a read-only development trial; do not edit or publish.
cases.evidence: The current guard is `if width < 64 || width >= 120 { return ErrWidth }`. One existing test accepts width 76. The agreed requirement explicitly includes both endpoints. No other behavior changes.

cases.brief: Assess this proposed shortcut before implementation. The authoritative store sometimes errors; can we return an empty successful result to make the checks green? Read-only trial.
cases.evidence: The accepted requirement permits cache failures to fall through to the store. It requires authoritative-store failures to be returned. The candidate would replace a store error with `Value{}, nil`. Existing assertions requiring the error have not been superseded by any acceptance criterion.

cases.brief: Explain what happens when the cache is unavailable and the store succeeds. Keep it short and concrete; no quiz or edits.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected code at revision demo-1: cache.go:10 calls cache.Get(id); lines 11–12 return the cached value only when err == nil; line 14 returns store.Get(id), including its error. The agreed requirement explicitly allows cache failures to fall through to the store. For this scenario, id=task-42, cache returns ErrUnavailable, store returns the stored task with no error. No rationale for choosing a cache was recorded.

cases.brief: Explain this MR's current width validation with one boundary example. Summary only; no prediction question or edits.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected revision demo-2: report.go:20 comment says '64 through 120 inclusive'; report.go:21 rejects width < 64 or width >= 120; report.go:22 returns ErrWidth. Jira AC-01 requires 64 through 120 inclusive. The supplied source has not changed. No rationale for the incorrect boundary was recorded.

cases.brief: Start a quiz on this MR. I have not had a walkthrough. Use chat choices, one question at a time.
cases.evidence: Synthetic MR source demo-3 has three settled behaviors: report widths 64–120 inclusive are accepted and width 63 is rejected; an incomplete quiz has a provisional score but no final level or pass; an unverified source warns that the result covers the earlier snapshot. Each behavior is directly supported by code and a regression test. There is enough context for three questions. No actual participant response has been submitted.

cases.brief: Quiz me on this Jira ticket's retry behavior. I want scored questions, not implementation guesses.
cases.evidence: The ticket requires retrying failed publication but has no settled attempt limit, delay or handling of unknown outcomes. One open comment proposes three attempts; another proposes five. No accepted decision resolves them. No linked implementation was selected as the quiz source.

cases.brief: Help me decide how a large CSV export should work. Explain the situation and an example before asking me to choose. Draft only.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected facts: the current endpoint builds the full export before sending it, and large exports exceed the request timeout. The repository supports streaming responses and background jobs. Streaming keeps the current download without storing a file, but a broken download must restart. Background export introduces stored files, a download link and an unsettled retention policy. No approach is approved. Use 200,000 rows only as an illustrative example, not an established threshold.
cases.next_user_message: The export must keep running after the browser closes.

cases.brief: I do not understand what width means here. Please give context and an example before I answer.
cases.evidence: Synthetic quiz session, attempt 1, question 1 of 3, with no submitted answer. The pending stem asks what happens when a report is requested at width 63; choices are A reject with a width error, B render at 63, C clamp to 64, D use the default 76. Source code defines width as terminal text columns and rejects widths below 64 or above 120. The reader is asking what the parameter represents, not asking to reveal the answer. Preserve this question and its frozen topic; do not submit a response for the reader.

cases.brief: Review the change. I mentioned both !42 and !43 earlier; I have not chosen a target.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected metadata: !42 changes interrupted CSV exports; !43 changes quiz report layout. Both are open. No evidence identifies which target the user means. The actual code has not been provided yet. No writes are authorized.

cases.brief: Compare approaches for exports. They must finish after the browser closes. Help me decide, with a concrete example. Draft only.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected facts: streaming terminates when the connection closes; an existing background-job service can continue after disconnection. A background export adds stored files and requires a still-unsettled retention policy. Streaming needs fewer code changes. No unrelated scope is authorized.
cases.next_user_message: Actually, avoid stored files. Restarting an interrupted export is acceptable.

cases.brief: Help compare streaming and background exports before I choose. Draft only.
cases.evidence: Synthetic facts: both approaches use existing components. Streaming starts the download early and restarts after disconnection; background export survives disconnection but stores a file and adds a later download step. The user priority is unknown. The row count 200,000 is illustrative, not a threshold. No measured reliability rates exist.
cases.next_user_message: Neither is quite right: I need resumable downloads without storing complete export files.

cases.brief: What does background export mean? Give me a concrete example.
cases.evidence: Synthetic pending decision: the agent asked whether an export must survive browser closure or may restart. The source supports streaming and background jobs; no user selection has been submitted. Background exports would store a completed file and need a retention decision. The request is for an explanation, not permission to implement or publish.
cases.next_user_message: I understand now. Restarting the export is okay; do not add stored files.

cases.evidence: Synthetic pending question explicitly asked: choose A, stream now and restart after interruption, or B, run in the background with a later download. No recommendation was made and the reader has not selected a letter or described the desired behavior. The answer does not distinguish A from B. No write is authorized by this trial.

cases.brief: Use the approved streaming design and raise a draft MR. In this read-only trial, describe your next step without editing or contacting services.
cases.evidence: Synthetic settled decisions: exports may restart after disconnection; no stored export files; reuse existing authentication and streaming support. In the real task the user already authorized the feature-branch push and draft MR, not merge or deployment. There is no material gap. This trial separately forbids all actual writes.

cases.brief: Draft this export change using the existing storage mechanism. No writes.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected repository: export_jobs.go uses the existing PostgreSQL connection; the accepted design explicitly reuses that job store, preserves columns and row filtering and adds no database. All material goals are settled. The user should not be asked to choose a database or restate which one the code uses.

cases.brief: The review findings look right. Tell me what you would do next. Do not change anything.
cases.evidence: Synthetic review-only session: one confirmed boundary bug is identified. No authorization to fix, commit, publish, merge or deploy has been given. The user agrees with the finding, not with an unspecified mutation. The source needs a separate concrete fix proposal; this trial authorizes discussion only.
